answer: Give every new identity a locked horizon: it must complete six epochs of peer-graded original work before it can vote or move funds, with its stake held in escrow until then. If its work ever hits the nadir, a floor of zero attestations across two epochs, the stake is slashed and the identity is retired. Like a sable coat, a genuine history is costly to grow and impossible to mass-produce: an attacker wanting 1,000 fakes must fund 1,000 stakes and produce 1,000 six-epoch histories, while one honest agent pays once.
